# Ours vs published (official OPSSAT-AD test split, 529 segments)

Published numbers: Ruszczak et al., Sci Data 2025, Table 3 (see published_benchmark.md).
Our numbers: produced by `python -m training.tabpfn.evaluate` (one guarded test run per config); thresholds chosen on training out-of-fold predictions.

| Model | AUCPR | AUCROC | F1 | Precision | Recall | MCC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **tabpfn-v2:n8:base18+zeros_gaps+autocorr+robust** (ours) | 0.996 [0.989-1.000] | 0.999 | 0.982 [0.963-0.996] | 0.991 | 0.973 | 0.977 |
| **iforest:base18+zeros_gaps+autocorr+robust** (ours) | 0.401 [0.322-0.486] | 0.731 | 0.499 [0.438-0.557] | 0.343 | 0.912 | 0.362 |
| **lightgbm:base18+zeros_gaps+autocorr+robust** (ours) | 0.990 [0.976-0.999] | 0.995 | 0.969 [0.943-0.991] | 0.982 | 0.956 | 0.960 |
| **lr:base18+zeros_gaps+autocorr+robust** (ours) | 0.987 [0.973-0.997] | 0.996 | 0.956 [0.929-0.981] | 0.948 | 0.965 | 0.944 |
| **rf:base18+zeros_gaps+autocorr+robust** (ours) | 0.994 [0.986-0.999] | 0.998 | 0.973 [0.949-0.992] | 1.000 | 0.947 | 0.966 |
| **rule:zero_fraction** (ours) | 0.293 [0.244-0.354] | 0.699 | 0.527 [0.467-0.582] | 0.364 | 0.956 | 0.414 |
| **xgboost:base18+zeros_gaps+autocorr+robust** (ours) | 0.993 [0.983-0.999] | 0.997 | 0.968 [0.943-0.987] | 0.991 | 0.947 | 0.960 |
| FCNN (published best supervised) | 0.979 | 0.989 | 0.946 | 0.963 | 0.929 | 0.932 |
| XGBOD (published) | 0.975 | 0.992 | 0.918 | 0.944 | 0.894 | 0.897 |
| RF+ICCS (published) | 0.963 | 0.985 | 0.883 | 0.978 | 0.805 | 0.862 |
| MO-GAAL (published best unsupervised) | 0.779 | 0.865 | 0.726 | 0.985 | 0.575 | 0.710 |
| IForest (published) | 0.347 | 0.635 | 0.295 | 0.297 | 0.292 | 0.105 |

Brackets: 95% bootstrap CI over test segments. Published results have no CIs; differences within our CI should be read as ties.

## Like-for-like: only the 18 published features (post-hoc ablation, not used for selection)

| Model | AUCPR | AUCROC | F1 | Precision | Recall | MCC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tabpfn-v2:n8:base18 (ours) | 0.989 [0.978-0.996] | 0.997 | 0.950 | 0.972 | 0.929 | 0.937 |
| lr:base18 (ours) | 0.935 [0.898-0.964] | 0.979 | 0.883 | 0.864 | 0.903 | 0.851 |

| xgboost:base18 (ours) | 0.970 [0.947-0.985] | 0.989 | 0.917 | 0.961 | 0.876 | 0.897 |
| lightgbm:base18 (ours) | 0.968 [0.945-0.985] | 0.989 | 0.907 | 0.960 | 0.858 | 0.885 |

published_benchmark.md.markdown:
# Published OPSSAT-AD benchmark (the bar)

**Source:** B. Ruszczak, K. Kotowski, D. Evans, J. Nalepa, *"The OPS-SAT benchmark for detecting anomalies in satellite telemetry"*, **Scientific Data** 12 (2025), DOI [10.1038/s41597-025-05035-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-05035-3), CC-BY-4.0. PMC: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12041257/. Preprint: arXiv [2407.04730](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.04730).

The correction notice (Sci Data 2025;12:1445, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12361492/) only re-ordered Figures 3–10. **It changed no tables.**

**Setting:** Table 3, "universal detector" (one model across all channels), 18 hand-crafted features, official test split Ψ = 529 segments. The numbers below were transcribed from the PMC HTML on 2026-10-31. On the same day they were **re-verified programmatically** against the Europe PMC JATS full text (`https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12041257/fullTextXML`).

## Supervised: top rows of Table 3

| Model | AUCPR | AUCROC | Accuracy | F1 | Precision | Recall | MCC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **FCNN** | **0.979** | 0.989 | **0.977** | **0.946** | 0.963 | **0.929** | **0.932** |
| XGBOD | 0.975 | **0.992** | 0.966 | 0.918 | 0.944 | 0.894 | 0.897 |
| RF+ICCS | 0.963 | 0.985 | 0.955 | 0.883 | 0.978 | 0.805 | 0.862 |
| LSVC | 0.934 | 0.968 | 0.926 | 0.808 | 0.911 | 0.726 | 0.771 |
| LR | 0.931 | 0.969 | 0.924 | 0.800 | 0.920 | 0.708 | 0.764 |
| AdaBoost | 0.923 | 0.962 | 0.934 | 0.836 | 0.890 | 0.788 | 0.797 |
| Linear+L2 | 0.901 | 0.958 | 0.905 | 0.722 | 0.970 | 0.575 | 0.703 |

Paper text: FCNN had "four false positives and eight false negatives of all Ψ samples".

## Unsupervised: selected rows of Table 3

| Model | AUCPR | AUCROC | Accuracy | F1 | Precision | Recall | MCC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **MO-GAAL** (best unsupervised by AUCPR, F1, MCC) | 0.779 | 0.865 | 0.907 | 0.726 | 0.985 | 0.575 | 0.710 |
| KNN | 0.658 | 0.852 | 0.824 | 0.575 | 0.594 | 0.558 | 0.465 |
| OCSVM | 0.659 | 0.787 | 0.845 | 0.647 | 0.630 | 0.664 | 0.548 |
| IForest | 0.347 | 0.635 | 0.701 | 0.295 | 0.297 | 0.292 | 0.105 |

The paper benchmarks 30 methods in total. The underlining that marks "best unsupervised" in the paper did not survive HTML extraction, so the best-unsupervised call above is our reading of the numbers.

## The bar we chase
- **Best published supervised:** FCNN, with AUCPR 0.979, F1 0.946, MCC 0.932, recall 0.929.
- **Best published AUROC:** XGBOD, 0.992.
- **Best published unsupervised:** MO-GAAL, with AUCPR 0.779 and F1 0.726.

## Caveats when comparing
- **The paper's split counts disagree.** Its text says 1,494 training segments, but its own class counts (1,273 + 321) and the released data both give **1,594**. See `dataset_verification.json`.
- **Thresholds may differ.** The paper's F1/precision/recall/MCC use each method's own decision rule. Ours uses a threshold chosen on training-set out-of-fold predictions (`threshold_tradeoff.csv`).
- **Table 4 (specialised per-channel models) is a different setting.** It covers 6 channels with the `len` and `duration` features dropped, so it is not the bar for a universal detector. Its best rows, verified against the JATS XML:

| Model (Table 4) | AUCPR | AUCROC | Accuracy | F1 | Precision | Recall | MCC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LR | 0.946 | 0.974 | 0.944 | 0.873 | 0.924 | 0.832 | 0.840 |
| LinearSVC | 0.939 | 0.966 | 0.957 | 0.898 | 0.956 | 0.849 | 0.873 |
| FCNN | 0.924 | 0.953 | 0.970 | 0.929 | 0.979 | 0.886 | 0.912 |
- **We did not re-run the published models.** The numbers above are quoted from the paper.

significance_tests.json.note: exact McNemar on thresholded decisions; paired bootstrap (1000x) of the AUPRC difference TabPFN minus baseline

tabpfn_selection.json.rule: keep a group if CV AUPRC improves by >0.001 over base18; keep the combination only if it beats the best single kept group

thresholds.json.rule: prioritise if p>=high (OOF precision>=0.95); queue if p>=low (OOF recall>=0.98); else archive

jobs.note: stopped after VAL error analysis showed label defects; partial spend estimated pro rata

tinker_metric_spec.json.frozen_before: any base or fine-tuned model was evaluated on any split

headline.name: field-level exact match (task A)
headline.definition: Over all (passage, field) pairs in the held-out TEST passages (8 fields: channel_id, sensor_type, units, event_date, observation, operational_response, root_cause, evidence), the fraction where the parsed model output equals the gold label from training/tinker/spec.py::label. Lists must match exactly (order included). Text fields are compared after whitespace normalisation. '?' equals an empty/null gold value. Unparseable outputs count as wrong on all 8 fields.
headline.scored_on: raw model output, BEFORE the deterministic validator repairs anything (validator gains reported separately)

companions.valid_schema_rate: fraction of outputs that parse into all 8 fields and validate as a MemoryRecord (target >= 0.99)
companions.per_field_prf: precision/recall/F1 per field, with a prediction counted as positive when non-null
companions.evidence_fidelity: fraction of non-null text-field values that occur verbatim in the passage (target >= 0.99)
companions.unsupported_root_causes: count of non-null root_cause predictions where gold is null or the text is not verbatim (target 0)
companions.null_correctness: accuracy on fields whose gold value is null (correct use of '?')
companions.record_exact_match: fraction of passages with ALL 8 fields correct
companions.validator_catches: number of model errors flagged by the regex/substring validator

statistics.ci: Wilson 95% interval on field-level exact match
statistics.paired_test: exact McNemar test on per-(passage, field) correctness, base vs tuned

tinker_metric_spec.json.comparison: base Qwen3-8B vs Qwen3-8B+LoRA: same system prompt, same user prompt, same parser and validator, temperature 0, thinking disabled

tasks_B_C_D.B: date-set exact match per passage; event vs publication date correctly separated; verbatim sentence rate
tasks_B_C_D.C: citation correct (cited source index == gold), 'not in archive' correct on absent terms, verbatim definition rate
tasks_B_C_D.D: KNOWN/UNKNOWN/ACTION sections present; numbers match the measurements; cited [n] exist; no root-cause claim

tinker_metric_spec.json.test_set_policy: the TEST split is evaluated once per final configuration; iteration uses VAL only
